Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the candid questions from your infra/security and platform teams. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from demo:
- Showed Redwood Private (VPC + optional on-prem package) and how the control plane vs data plane separation works.
- Walked through our latency/cost tradeoffs and the model variants we recommend for production inference.
- Covered basic networking topologies (VPC peering, private link, and air-gapped on-prem).

Open questions you raised:
1) How Redwood compares to hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS/GCP) for private deployments — control, latency, egress.
2) Whether we can run fully air-gapped (no outbound control plane) for regulated workloads.
3) Networking requirements and whether we need NAT/egress for model updates or telemetry.

Proposed next tests:
- Short latency/throughput run against your test workload (1k reqs, seq lengths ~512) on our private node in your VPC.
- Security evidence bundle review (SOC2 artifacts, KMS/HSM integration notes).
- Air-gapped feasibility assessment: we can run an offline installer in your lab and validate model sync procedures.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_fintechco.xlsx (MVP scope + timeline), high-level networking doc attached as PDF.

Can you confirm availability next week for the perf run and who on your side should be the technical contact for the air-gap test? If you prefer, we can also prepare a short one-pager explicitly comparing Redwood Private vs AWS Managed Endpoints / Vertex AI / other inference APIs focused on private deployments.

Thanks —

Thanks Sarah — looping in Rishi (security) and Dev (deploy) to answer the technical items.

A few quick differentiators we’ll include in the one-pager:
- Control plane separation: optional private control plane or customer-managed control plane for Private customers. In practice this means you can run the data plane entirely in your VPC/on-prem with no inbound connectivity from the public internet.
- Deterministic egress: telemetry is off by default for Private; we provide a signed, configurable telemetry agent and you can disable it completely in air-gapped mode.
- Model parity & performance: our optimized runtime narrows latency gaps vs hyperscaler endpoints and often beats managed endpoints for tail latency on GPU-backed instances because of KV-cache and batching optimizations.
- Packaging: we support a fully offline installer + signed model bundle for air-gapped installs; we’ll share a runbook.

Rishi / Dev — can you confirm the offline installer constraints (size, how model updates are signed and applied) and whether we need outbound access to Redwood for licensing or can we run with an on-prem license server?

Action items for us: we’ll send the one-pager and a short SOC2/security evidence summary, and prepare a perf run plan for Noah. Proposed perf window: Tue 24 Feb, 09:00–12:00 PT. Does that work for FintechCo?

-Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood Private — Post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Sarah/Marissa,

Happy to break this down from a security and network perspective. High-level answers below; attaching a short PDF with network diagrams and the security evidence summary.

1) Air-gapped deployment: supported. We provide an offline install tarball (~2.3GB for the runtime + base toolchain) plus signed model bundles. Model updates are delivered as signed artifacts; you validate signatures with a root CA we provide or your own. No outbound connectivity required for runtime or model inference. For model license checks, we support an on-prem license server (HTTPS) or an offline license file with per-deployment expiry — your choice.

2) Telemetry & egress: telemetry is opt-in. By default logging/telemetry endpoints are disabled; if enabled they can be routed through a customer-managed proxy. For strict customers we provide a 'no-telemetry' mode that removes external endpoints and writes logs to customer-managed S3/NFS.

3) Control plane & model sync: two modes — managed control plane (Redwood-hosted) where the control plane speaks to your VPC over private link, or customer-managed control plane where you run the control plane in your account. For air-gapped customers we recommend the latter; model sync is performed via signed bundles delivered by secure transfer (SCP or physical media).

4) Network requirements for perf run: for the VPC mode we ask for a private endpoint (VPC peering or PrivateLink) and a small outbound permission during initial bootstrap for host key exchange if you choose managed control plane. If you want zero egress, choose customer-managed control plane + on-prem license file.

Known comparisons vs hyperscalers (brief):
- AWS/GCP managed endpoints: good SLA and scale but limited control over kernel/runtime selection, less predictable tail latency for long-context workloads, and less straightforward air-gap/offline options.
- Hyperscaler BYO models: you can sometimes self-host on cloud VMs but you lose the inference runtime optimizations (KV cache, continuous batching) unless you build that layer yourself.

I’ll be looking for Noah’s contact info for coordinating the perf run and can provide temporary credentials for the VPC test node.

-Rishi
Head of Security & Platform Compliance
Redwood Inference

Sarah — quick technical note on the offline installer and on-prem packaging:

- Installer: we provide a tarball that contains the runtime binaries, container images, and a bootstrap script. For fully air-gapped installs we provide SHA256 sums and PGP signatures for all artifacts. Typical install time on a 16-core host with 4xA100 is ~45–60 mins.
- Model bundles: delivered as signed tar.gz files. Updates can be staged in a staging namespace and then promoted.
- Control plane: customer-managed control plane runs as a small k8s deployment (3 control-plane pods; minimal external dependencies). We can give an example helm chart.
- Licensing: on-prem license file mode works without any outbound access; if you prefer centralized license management we can also run a license server in your VPC.

I’ll attach a small runbook and the helm chart snippet to the drive link Marissa shared.

-Dev
